clue.text: Party platform given by chairman defending Ulster party?

indicators.note: defending means wrapping protectively round, so the chairman's letters go outside

parts.note: Chairman Mao, the Chinese leader
NI is Northern Ireland, often called Ulster
a fest is a festive party or gathering

explanation.surface: A political manifesto is presented by a party chairman protecting a Northern Irish faction.
explanation.definitionFit: A published statement of a party's policies is its platform, a synonym in political usage.

clue.text: Fruit found in some London markets

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A fruit sold on stalls in various London markets.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sweet fruit with a hard rind, as in honeydew or watermelon, is an example of fruit.

clue.text: Poor Finn treated before time — it's typical of a charity?

indicators.note: before places the shuffled letters ahead of the time letter
treated means processed or worked on, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An impoverished Finn gets help ahead of time, as a charity might provide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' turns POOR FINN into NONPROFI, which comes 'before' T.
explanation.definitionFit: Charities are run not to make money for owners, so the adjective describes their typical status.

clue.text: Repetitive element in river parking soon to be scrapped

indicators.note: in places the repeating sound inside the river and parking letters

parts.note: the Forth is a Scottish river
P is the map and road-sign abbreviation for parking
an echo is a sound that repeats itself

explanation.surface: Something repetitive in a riverside car park that is about to be demolished.
explanation.walkthrough: The Forth is the river flowing past Edinburgh into the Firth of Forth.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something or someone about to be axed or got rid of.

clue.text: Model with male in Greek island — a TV staple?

parts.note: to sit is to pose as a model for an artist

indicators.note: in puts the male letter inside the island's name

parts.note: Cos (or Kos) is an island in the Dodecanese

explanation.surface: A model and a man on a Greek island, as though a holiday programme on television.
explanation.definitionFit: Situation comedies are a regular fixture of television schedules, hence a staple.

clue.text: Son seen to fragment unity

indicators.note: to fragment is to break into pieces, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A son is seen to break up the family's unity.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony is that the surface talks of breaking unity while the anagram builds a word for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being one whole, undivided, is a synonym of unity.

clue.text: Crash arose with sun obscured

indicators.note: obscured means hidden from view, so the sun's letter disappears from the word

parts.note: sprang means leapt up or arose

explanation.surface: A crash happened when the sun was blotted out.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is British slang for a minor car crash or bump.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquial British word for a vehicle collision, a synonym of crash.

clue.text: Take a look at food on way up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the letters bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: keep is board and food, as in earning one's keep

explanation.surface: Glancing at a dish as it is carried upstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick sly glance is a brief look, so the verb means to glance.

clue.text: Current pair featuring in a paper

indicators.note: featuring in means appearing within, so the pair goes inside

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper
in cricket a pair is two ducks, scores of nothing, written as two O's

explanation.surface: A couple are featured in a newspaper's current affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'pair' in cricket is a batter out for nought in both innings: two ducks, two O's.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in progress or underway is current, a synonym.

clue.text: Bandit, familiar figure in jungle reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard or spoken, so the word is matched by its sound

parts.note: the great ape is a well-known jungle animal

explanation.surface: A bandit is a well-known character hiding out in the jungle, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: An irregular fighter is loosely a bandit or outlaw, a looser synonym.

clue.text: Solitary figure still on errand partly

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A solitary person still out running an errand.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps to themselves is a solitary figure, a direct description.

clue.text: Word of sympathy supporting European consequently

parts.note: 'there, there' is said to comfort someone
to be for something is to support it

explanation.surface: A comforting word backing a European, and so it follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean as a result or for that reason, synonyms.

clue.text: It's foolish to rank hero in Asian country

indicators.note: foolish suggests letters behaving senselessly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ranking a hero in an Asian country is foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: The state on the northern Korean peninsula is an example of an Asian country.

clue.text: Prison disturbance

explanation.surface: A disturbance inside a prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for jail, and also a commotion or fuss: two separate senses.

clue.text: Complex book kept by enthusiast in school

indicators.note: kept by means held within, so the book goes inside
in puts the enthusiast inside the school

parts.note: a coed is a mixed school
a nut is a fanatic, as in a fitness nut
VOL is short for volume, a book

explanation.surface: A difficult book held by a keen pupil at school.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions nest: 'in' builds CONUTED first, then 'kept by' slots the book inside that. A coed is a mixed school, chiefly American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Convoluted means intricate and hard to follow, a synonym of complex.

clue.text: Cousin abroad entertaining fellow with a clear outline

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the fellow is held inside
abroad suggests being all over the place, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cousin overseas hosts a friend who has a clear profile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' turns COUSIN into INOCUS; 'entertaining' puts F inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharply defined image has crisp edges, a fair paraphrase.

clue.text: Home supporter with headwear is childish

parts.note: in means at home
a fan is a supporter
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A fan at a home match wearing a hat is behaving like a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Infantile behaviour is babyish, a synonym of childish.

clue.text: Clio sat composed and uncomplaining

indicators.note: composed means put together, so these letters are assembled anew

explanation.surface: Clio sat calmly without a grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' also looks like part of the definition, meaning calm, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Enduring hardship without protest is the philosophical sense, a synonym.

clue.text: Roman and Croat at sea missing a seabird

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are mixed up
missing means lacking, so one letter is left out of the pool

explanation.surface: A Roman and a Croat sailing without a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges ROMAN CROAT with one A 'missing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A large black diving bird of coasts is an example of a seabird.

clue.text: Rich university attracting old American that's stupid

indicators.note: attracting means drawing alongside, so these letters are added on

parts.note: fat means rich, as in a fat salary
US means American

explanation.surface: A wealthy university drawing in an aged American who is stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatuous means silly and pointless, a synonym of stupid.

clue.text: A route fringed by revolutionary workers showing endurance

indicators.note: fringed by means bordered on each side, so the workers go round
revolutionary means turning over, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: ants are worker insects
the M1 is a British motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A road lined by rebellious labourers showing stamina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' gives STNA. The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds, so a route; 'fringed by' wraps STNA round A MI.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, a synonym of endurance.

clue.text: Tax reversed near exotic restaurant

indicators.note: reversed says the tax word is written backwards

parts.note: VAT is value added tax

indicators.note: exotic means strange or foreign, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tax turned around near an exotic eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' gives TAV; 'exotic' turns NEAR into ERNA.
explanation.definitionFit: A taverna is a small Greek eating house, an example of a restaurant.

clue.text: Elder, say, protecting first class new novice

indicators.note: protecting means covering round, so the tree goes outside

parts.note: the elder is an example of a tree
A1 means first class, written AI

explanation.surface: An elder looks after a promising newcomer, a novice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elder' looks like an older person but is the tree; 'say' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in training is a novice, a synonym.

clue.text: Observe bit of music

explanation.surface: Watching for a passage of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb meaning notice, and a single tone in music: two senses.

clue.text: Tour planned to cover Dutch house

indicators.note: to cover means to go round, so the shuffled letters enclose the Dutch letter
planned means organised or arranged, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A tour organised to take in a Dutch house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planned' turns TOUR into TUOR; 'to cover' puts D in it. 'Dutch house' tempts, but the house is royal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were an English royal dynasty, and a royal house is a dynasty.

clue.text: Dessert in a carrier left by one in area

indicators.note: in places the carrier, left and one inside the area word

parts.note: a zone is an area

indicators.note: by means next to, so these letters sit side by side

parts.note: a bag is something to carry things in
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pudding carried in a bag, left beside someone in a certain area.
explanation.walkthrough: Zabaglione is an Italian whipped dessert of egg yolks, sugar and Marsala.
explanation.definitionFit: A whipped Italian custard served as a pudding is an example of a dessert.

clue.text: Get rid of first of pollution in river and lake

indicators.note: in puts the picked letter inside the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Clearing pollution out of a river and lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in south-west England, flowing through Exeter.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to drive out or remove, a synonym.

clue.text: Mark award, nothing less

indicators.note: less means minus, so the nothing letter is taken away

parts.note: an Oscar is a film award
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Marking an award with nothing taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a lasting mark left on the skin, a synonym.

clue.text: Form of reasoning in prelude

definitions.meaning: logic that moves from particular cases to a general rule
an introductory or opening section, as before a play

explanation.surface: A method of reasoning set out in an introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferring general rules from instances, and also an introductory part: two senses.

clue.text: Hobo getting little money on public transport

indicators.note: on means placed after, as in an across entry

parts.note: a tram is a street railway vehicle
P is a penny, a small amount of money

explanation.surface: A vagrant earning small change on the bus or tram.
explanation.definitionFit: A homeless wanderer is a vagrant, a synonym.

clue.text: Troublesome child overlooking initial mistake

indicators.note: overlooking initial means ignoring the first letter, so it is dropped

parts.note: a little terror is a naughty child

explanation.surface: A naughty child ignoring an early mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Loan cadet arranged, based on hearsay

indicators.note: arranged means set out in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A loan to a cadet set up on the strength of gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence drawn from stories people tell rather than proof is hearsay-based.
